case_study_insert.main_stem: Auric & Sons Jewellers (ASJ) is a partnership in the high-street jewellery retail sector, employing a workforce of 26. Founded in 1987 by Yusuf and Leila Auric in Saltmere, and now managed by their son Darius, the firm operates a hierarchical organisational structure with autocratic leadership. ASJ plans to invest $700,000 in a bridal suite and certified watch workshop inside its Saltmere flagship, financed by a $450,000 ten-year bank loan and $250,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $275,000 a year, a variable cost of $180 a unit and a selling price of $230, and currently produces 11,000 units a year. ASJ faces a growing operational problem: a shortage of qualified watchmakers and goldsmiths, so the repair queue is lengthening.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Market Research Summary (October 2026): In a survey of 500 loyal clients, 72% said they would consider ASJ for engagement or wedding jewellery, 54% asked about certified watch servicing, and 33% follow ASJ on social media. Website enquiries rose 44% after the spring campaign, with 61% of visitors on mobile. The valuation counter issued 210 written valuations last year averaging $1,850. Repair turnaround averages 12 days; sizing-error complaints fell from 18 to 9 per month. Off-the-job watchmaker training at the Saltmere college costs $950 per employee, while on-the-job shadowing pairs apprentices with master jewellers.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Auric & Sons Jewellers as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.25% to 5.0%, raising the cost of variable-rate borrowing for long-term investments. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 7.5% from $12.00 to $12.90 per hour from April 2026. (3) The gold price rose 17.8% year-on-year and precious-metal input costs are up 15.2%, inflation is running at 3.6%, and consumer spending on luxury jewellery grew only 1.8% in the same period.

questions.question_text: ASJ plans to fund its $700,000 flagship expansion with a $450,000 bank loan and $250,000 retained profit. Explain two advantages for ASJ of using retained profit rather than an overdraft.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit carries no interest charge at all, whereas an overdraft is typically variable-rate and repayable on demand, which is dangerous now the central bank has lifted the base rate to 5.0% and ASJ's $450,000 loan already commits it to ten years of repayments. Keeping the $250,000 portion internal protects the partnership's $275,000 fixed-cost base and leaves headroom if bridal demand disappoints or gold pushes the $180 variable cost higher still.

Point 2: Funding the bridal suite and certified watch workshop from retained profit keeps the expansion entirely under the Auric family's control, with no bank able to renegotiate facilities if luxury spending grows only 1.8% or if gold keeps climbing. For a partnership about to market certified watch servicing, which 54% of loyal clients already asked about, covenant-free funding reassures staff and clients that the workshop, apprentice pipeline and new bridal collection can be delivered on schedule, without the administrative burden and personal-asset exposure an overdraft would add to a family firm.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of retained profit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to Auric & Sons Jewellers and its flagship expansion.

questions.question_text: ASJ is launching its bridal suite. Consider national television advertising, a print jewellery catalogue posted to loyal clients, or social media advertising. Which should ASJ choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
National television advertising: TV would dramatise the bridal suite to a huge audience and could make ASJ a household name beyond Saltmere, building aspirational brand equity at speed. But a single-flagship jeweller making 11,000 units a year would be buying national reach it cannot fulfil from one store, and the production and airtime costs are unjustifiable against a $700,000 project funded partly from retained profit with gold prices rising 17.8% year-on-year.

Print jewellery catalogue for loyal clients: A posted catalogue targets clients with proven wealth, lists the $1,850-average valuation service beautifully, and suits older buyers who have bought wedding jewellery from the family for decades. However it costs print and postage per client, is slow to update once gold prices move, and younger engaged couples increasingly begin their search on Instagram and Google rather than reading posted catalogues.

Social media advertising: ASJ can target couples in Saltmere and nearby towns searching engagement content, showcase the suite and certified pieces visually, and retarget website visitors; 61% of its enquiry traffic is already on mobile after a campaign that lifted enquiries 44%, and 33% of loyal clients follow ASJ on social channels, so the seed audience already exists for lookalike targeting.

Recommendation: ASJ should choose social media advertising. It converts the 44% enquiry momentum and mobile-first traffic into booked suite appointments, reaches younger engaged couples at a fraction of TV's cost, and fits the existing 33% social following. Television is rejected as untargeted and unaffordable for a single Saltmere flagship; the print catalogue is rejected as the lead channel because it reaches only existing clients too slowly to build launch buzz, though a small mailer to the valuation list would complement the digital push rather than replace it.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited knowledge or outline of the promotional options with minimal application to ASJ.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of ASJ with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options in the context of ASJ with a well-justified recommendation explaining why television and the print catalogue are rejected as lead channels.

questions.question_text: ASJ faces a shortage of qualified watchmakers and goldsmiths. Explain two benefits for ASJ of using on-the-job shadowing with master jewellers to build the apprentice skills pipeline.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Shadowing transfers irreplaceable bench craft, sizing, stone setting, movement service and gold finishing, directly from master jewellers to apprentices in the workshop, preserving standards that a generic college course cannot teach on vintage pieces. Trainees learn ASJ's exact quality protocols on real client watches and rings, shortening the 12-day repair turnaround and raising client trust at precisely the moment the certified watch workshop is about to open.

Point 2: On-the-job shadowing is the cheapest route to the skills ASJ needs, costing nothing beyond the $950 college fee if an apprentice later takes external certification, and it keeps apprentices productive from week one while recruitment drags on. It also deepens loyalty, which matters in a craft trade where trained staff are scarce; apprentices invested in by the Auric family are far less likely to leave for a rival. The risk is slow transfer if master jewellers are diverted from paying repair work, so ASJ must schedule shadowing around the 12-day queue rather than on top of it.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of on-the-job shadowing/training identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to ASJ's skills gap, repair queue and workshop launch.

questions.question_text: ASJ must train staff for the certified watch workshop. Consider on-the-job shadowing in the workshop or off-the-job training at the Saltmere college. Which should ASJ choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job shadowing: Pairing trainees with master jewellers is bench-specific, immediate and fee-free, covering movement diagnosis, regulation and case finishing on ASJ's actual client watches and jewellery. It keeps the 12-day repair turnaround intact during the transition and feeds directly into the certified workshop's launch, because masters transmit the exact quality checks ASJ promises. Its limits are that masters lose selling and repair time while coaching, and no external certificate is gained, which slightly weakens the 'certified' marketing claim to sceptical clients.

Off-the-job training: The Saltmere college course at $950 per employee provides certified watchmaker modules and a recognised credential, strengthening the workshop's 'certified' claim exactly where 54% of loyal clients have already shown interest in servicing. If all 26 employees attended (an upper bound; only workshop staff need it), fees would total $24,700 (26 x $950), and being off-site also removes staff from the sales floor and bench, lengthening the 12-day queue and the sizing service precisely when bridal demand builds toward the suite launch. Content is generic, so it would still need tailoring to ASJ's archive, tooling and client base.

Decision: ASJ should choose on-the-job shadowing as the core, sending the lead watchmaker and one apprentice to the college for certification. Shadowing is cheaper, bench-specific and protects continuity of the 12-day service; full off-the-job training is rejected because $24,700 in fees plus lost bench time strains the $275,000 fixed-cost base during the $700,000 fit-out, and generic modules would still need customising to ASJ's craft standards anyway. The reasoning rests on continuity: shadowing lets masters supervise work on live repairs so the queue keeps moving, whereas the college certification is a one-off intake that yields no daily practice on the repair turnaround, so the deciding consideration is continuity of service during the fit-out rather than the credential alone.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to ASJ.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of one or both training methods in the context of ASJ.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both training methods in the context of ASJ with a well-justified decision covering cost, bench disruption and workshop relevance.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how ASJ's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs / Contribution per unit. Substitution: $275,000 / ($230 - $180) = $275,000 / $50 = 5,500 units. Answer: break-even output is 5,500 units a year.

sub_parts.question_text: Calculate ASJ's unit cost at 11,000 units.
sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Unit cost = (Fixed costs + (Variable cost per unit x Output)) / Output. Substitution: ($275,000 + ($180 x 11,000)) / 11,000 = ($275,000 + $1,980,000) / 11,000 = $2,255,000 / 11,000 = $205. Answer: unit cost is $205 a unit.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways ASJ's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. ASJ can compare the 5,500-unit break-even output with its 11,000-unit output, a margin of safety of 5,500 units (exactly 50% of output), showing the flagship clears its fixed costs comfortably even before the bridal suite opens.
2. The $50 contribution per unit lets managers test the effect of precious-metal inflation; if the $180 variable cost rises by 15.2%, contribution falls to about $22.64 (15.2% x $180 = $27.36), signalling urgent re-pricing or supplier renegotiation before the suite's launch pricing is locked in.
3. Knowing break-even output lets ASJ stress-test the $450,000 bank loan; at 5,500 units ASJ exactly covers the $275,000 fixed costs, so managers can model whether a 20% demand drop to 8,800 units still services the loan, using the margin of safety as the tripwire for cost action.
4. Managers can track unit cost ($205 at 11,000 units) across gold cycles and compare it with the $230 average price to protect positioning, and use it to decide whether workshop servicing should carry a labour-based margin closer to the bridal trade rather than the product margin norm.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 5,500 units | (ii) Unit cost = $205 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety vs 11,000-unit output; gold-price stress test on the $50 contribution; loan stress-testing at the 5,500-unit break-even point; and unit-cost tracking at $205 to protect positioning.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate ASJ's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has ASJ's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.24 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.27 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 0.43 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 0.45 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $420,000 inventories + $130,000 trade receivables + $95,000 cash = $645,000; 2025 current assets = $520,000 + $210,000 + $80,000 = $810,000. Ratio 2024 = $645,000 / $520,000 = 1.24; 2025 = $810,000 / $640,000 = 1.27. Excluding inventories: 2024 = ($645,000 - $420,000) / $520,000 = $225,000 / $520,000 = 0.43; 2025 = ($810,000 - $520,000) / $640,000 = $290,000 / $640,000 = 0.45.

Evaluation: The position has improved only modestly and the quick measure remains uncomfortably low. The excess of current assets over current liabilities rose from 1.24 to 1.27 and the stock-free measure improved from 0.43 to 0.45. Cash actually fell from $95,000 to $80,000 while current liabilities grew from $520,000 to $640,000, inventories were built up from $420,000 to $520,000 ahead of the gold-price rise and the $700,000 build, and trade receivables jumped from $130,000 to $210,000; stock and tied-up cash in receivables are absorbing most of the gains.

Conclusion: ASJ's financial position has improved, but only modestly and it remains fragile. The current ratio (1.24 to 1.27) and the acid test ratio (0.43 to 0.45) both ticked up, yet neither clears conventional comfort levels, and the improvement sits on an inventory build that must convert into bridal and watch sales before the suite opens. ASJ should tighten bridal deposit collection, watch receivables from valuation and repair customers, avoid any further commitments until the $450,000 loan instalments are serviced comfortably, and treat the ratios as a warning rather than a green light for additional borrowing.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the current ratio and acid test ratio for both 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratio calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of inventories, receivables, cash and liabilities movements and a justified conclusion on whether ASJ's financial position improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for ASJ of opening a certified watch workshop in its flagship.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Certified servicing converts the 54% of loyal clients who asked about watch servicing into high-trust, recurring revenue, with after-care visits that keep ASJ top of mind when clients later buy engagement or anniversary jewellery. A certification credential supports premium labour pricing, builds the craft apprenticeship pipeline ASJ urgently lacks to fix the 12-day repair queue, and differentiates the flagship from discount online sellers while luxury spending grows only 1.8%; a visible in-store atelier also strengthens walk-in bridal conversion from the 72% who would consider ASJ for rings.

Disadvantage: The workshop needs certified watchmakers whom ASJ currently lacks, and the 12-day repair turnaround could lengthen during the fit-out, souring the very loyal clients it aims to serve; mistakes on high-value customer pieces risk compensation claims and reputational damage out of all proportion to the repair fee. Equipment, certification and apprentice wages inflate the $275,000 fixed-cost base and the $700,000 project beyond the bridal suite alone, and a slow-starting workshop could drain cash while trade receivables already climbed from $130,000 to $210,000, tightening an already fragile quick measure of 0.45.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to ASJ's research data, repair queue and flagship expansion.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 5.0%, the 7.5% minimum wage increase and the 15.2% rise in precious-metal input costs will affect ASJ. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.25% to 5.0%): If ASJ's $450,000 ten-year bank loan is variable-rate, each 0.25% costs 0.0025 x $450,000 = $1,125 a year, so the full 0.75% rise adds $3,375 a year (0.0075 x $450,000). That is tolerable against $275,000 of fixed costs, but material if gold also forces higher working-capital borrowing to hold stock; fixing the rate now is prudent, and any future top-up borrowing for the $700,000 build becomes more expensive.

Minimum wage increase (7.5%, to $12.90 per hour): ASJ's craft goldsmiths and watchmakers are paid well above the benchmark, but counter, cleaning and valuation-admin support staff are hourly-paid, so the rise still touches the payroll. Hours and exact pay rates are not stated in the insert, so no defensible annual total can be invented; at productivity of 11,000 units / 26 employees = 423.1 units per employee, the rise is absorbable if bridal and servicing volumes grow as planned, otherwise unit labour cost rises and the $180 variable cost effectively increases, squeezing the $50 contribution per unit.

Precious-metal input cost inflation (gold up 17.8% year-on-year; inputs up 15.2%): As an explicit upper bound, if the full $180 variable cost tracked input inflation it would add $27.36 per unit (0.152 x $180); at 11,000 units a year that is about $301,000 a year, cutting contribution from $50 toward about $22.64. Even partial pass-through is sobering. With luxury spending growing only 1.8%, ASJ cannot assume price rises will be absorbed silently; but the 44% enquiry surge, the 72% who would consider ASJ for rings, and gold indexing on staple lines give room to re-price with transparency and to resell customers on value rather than discounting.

Conclusion: The 15.2% rise in precious-metal input costs will have the greatest impact. It compounds across every one of the 11,000 units and every repair, unlike the $3,375 capped annual interest effect and the productivity-contingent wage rise, which is partly offset by above-benchmark craft pay. ASJ should pre-buy gold for staple lines, re-price via the bridal premium, negotiate loyalty deposits, and delay any further workshop beyond the current plan until input costs stabilise.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to ASJ.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on ASJ's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes in the context of ASJ with a well-justified judgement that precious-metal input-cost inflation has the greatest impact and why the other two are smaller.
